title: Dual Laser Triangulator
subtitle: Compact dual-line optical surface profiling
summary: I am building an ESP32-S3 and OV9281 module that measures printed surfaces from two projected laser lines and reports profiles over CAN bus.

content.body: I designed the instrument as a small printer-side measurement system rather than a general-purpose camera. The monochrome sensor observes both laser traces, while the local processing path reduces the captured strip into geometry useful to the printer.
The PCB combines camera power sequencing, the parallel image interface, laser control and the CAN transceiver within the mechanical limits of the optical assembly.

content.title: Current state
content.body: The design is complete and I am assembling the PCBs before optical alignment and end-to-end profiling tests.

title: Gigaplex
subtitle: A complete game console in a 15 × 11 matrix
summary: I designed a CR2032-powered keychain console with a charlieplexed display, five buttons, motion input and sound.

content.body: I reduced the interface to hardware that remains understandable at very low resolution: 165 LEDs, directional controls, one confirmation button and physical motion. The result is small enough to live on a keychain without turning every game into the same blinking square.
The firmware architecture separates matrix scanning, input polling, game state and buzzer timing so the tiny MCU can keep the display stable while games and IMU-driven effects run.

content.title: Current state
content.body: The electrical and mechanical design is finished, and I am now assembling the first PCBs.

title: Code-Less Dice
subtitle: Electronic randomness without a microcontroller
summary: I built an electronic die whose vibration-triggered 555 oscillator cycles six shift-register states before slowing to a stop.

content.body: A brief contact from the vibration switch charges the timing capacitor and starts the roll. The 555 initially clocks the state circuit quickly, then the rate falls with the capacitor voltage until one of the six LED patterns remains visible.

items.title: Initial build
items.body: I selected an HX 0805-C2 believing it was a passive vibration contact, but it was a tilt sensor that required active interpretation and could not trigger the circuit as intended.

items.title: Vibration-switch redesign
items.body: I replaced it with an SW-58010PZD-7N11S1 spring-contact vibration switch and formed its through-hole leads so the part could be mounted flat on the board.

content.title: Manufacturing result
content.body: The final circuit works and is assembled on my LumenPnP machine.

title: Lumen PnP Feeders
subtitle: Common hardware across four tape widths
summary: I redesigned the 16 mm and 24 mm LumenPnP feeders around the same hardware and electronics used by the 8 mm and 12 mm versions.

content.body: The open-source feeder family originally left the wider sizes with a different assembly burden. I adapted their mechanics so all four widths can share the proven smaller-feeder electronics and as much common hardware as practical.

rows.label: Primary goal
rows.value: Reduce electronics variation and assembly complexity

content.title: Designed, not yet validated
content.body: The shared architecture exists in CAD and PCB form, but it remains experimental until the wider feeders are assembled and tested with tape.

title: Filament Scale
subtitle: A standalone spool station with identity and history
summary: I built an ESP32-S3 filament scale that combines load-cell measurement, NFC spool binding, local records and Spoolman integration.

content.body: I wanted spool tracking to remain useful even when the printer or network was unavailable. The device therefore performs the weighing and identification locally, records transactions to removable storage and can synchronise with an existing Spoolman installation.

rows.label: Connectivity
rows.value: Local web interface and Spoolman synchronisation

content.body: The interface guides zeroing, calibration, spool selection and tag binding directly on the device, while the browser view handles configuration without making routine weighing dependent on a phone.

title: Smart Reflow Oven
subtitle: Repeatable reflow control with a platinum RTD
summary: I converted a reflow oven to use PT100 temperature feedback after an NTC-based approach proved too sensitive to drift.

content.body: The first sensing approach made calibration too dependent on thermistor behaviour at reflow temperatures. I changed the final design to a PT100 so the controller could work from a more stable and repeatable resistance curve.

rows.label: Reason for change
rows.value: Reduced drift and better behaviour at higher temperatures

content.title: Completed system
content.body: The PT100-based control system is the finished version of the oven.

title: Chroma Klipper
subtitle: Printer-side coordination for full-colour FDM
summary: I am developing the Klipper integration that coordinates ordinary print motion with colour output from the ChromaDye hardware.

content.body: This layer turns slicer output into printer behaviour. It has to keep colour deposition aligned with the same motion, timing and state transitions that already govern the underlying FDM print.

content.title: System position
content.description: The integration sits between colour-aware slicing and the physical deposition controller.

content.title: Dependency
content.body: Development remains active because meaningful printer tests depend on the ChromaDye integration becoming stable.

title: Chroma Slicer
subtitle: Colour-aware slicing from textured model to layer data
summary: I extended OrcaSlicer with a working full-colour pipeline for textured model import, colour-preserving geometry and per-layer raster generation.

content.body: Colour information normally disappears long before a conventional slicer produces toolpaths. I added a surface representation that keeps UV and texture data attached to model volumes so later stages can ask what colour belongs at each sampled point.

rows.label: Internal data
rows.value: Colour-aware surface data on model volumes

content.title: Feature complete
content.body: The end-to-end feature works, but I still consider it active while I improve robustness, persistence and integration with the rest of the Chroma toolchain.

title: ChromaDye
subtitle: Timing-critical colour deposition hardware
summary: I built the ESP32-S3 cartridge driver that converts colour data into constrained HP123 nozzle pulses for the full-colour printer.

content.body: The controller queues nozzle data and emits a parallel waveform whose pulse widths must stay inside the cartridge limits. The electrical interface is only half the problem; the same timing guarantees have to survive buffering, transfer and printer integration.

items.title: Hardware pulse-time limit
items.body: I first attempted to enforce the maximum firing time entirely in hardware, but that revision did not operate reliably.

items.title: Software-enforced limit
items.body: I moved pulse limiting into the output software and the revised electronics now appear to behave correctly on their own.

items.title: Full-system integration
items.body: The remaining work is connecting the stable hardware path to the slicer and printer control stack without losing timing or colour alignment.

content.title: Current blocker
content.body: The board-level behaviour is promising, but the project is still caught in integration work across the complete Chroma system.

title: Game Vault
subtitle: A room-based cooperative game for self-hosting
summary: I built a server-hosted cooperative game with multiplayer rooms, intended to run on a small SBC behind a Cloudflare Tunnel.

content.body: Players join a shared room and cooperate through a centrally hosted game session. I designed deployment around an SBC such as a Raspberry Pi so the server can remain physically local while the tunnel provides the external route.

content.title: Deployment path
content.description: The game keeps its state on the self-hosted server and exposes only the web connection through the tunnel.
items: Browser clients join a named room
The room runs on the local game server
Cloudflare Tunnel forwards the service without direct router exposure

content.body: The deliberately strange and generic naming originated as camouflage for very basic network filtering—sometimes the least suspicious protocol is apparently a boring noun.

title: Parametric EPaper Dashboard
subtitle: A JSON-composed image pipeline for low-power displays
summary: I wrote a Python and Pillow renderer whose JSON configuration assembles calendar, weather and other modules into one e-paper-ready image.

content.body: Instead of fixing the dashboard layout in one script, I made each section a module that reads its parameters from JSON, renders onto a transparent layer and composes itself onto the shared canvas.

content.title: Render pipeline
content.description: Configuration and live data are converted into independent visual layers before Pillow produces the final display bitmap.
items: JSON selects modules, positions and dimensions
Modules parse one or more calendar accounts or weather sources
Symbols and text are drawn onto separate layers
The layers are composited into the final image

rows.label: Schedules
rows.value: Events from one or more calendar accounts

rows.label: Layout
rows.value: Module placement and sizing controlled through JSON

rows.label: Output
rows.value: A composed image suitable for an e-paper display

title: Lucid Gloves Alternate Battery PCB
subtitle: Three revisions from bulky connector to onboard charging
summary: I redesigned the Lucid Gloves battery interface through PH, SH and charging-board versions until it fit the available space and workflow.

content.body: The board began as a connector substitution and became a compact battery subsystem. Each revision answered a physical issue from the previous one rather than adding features without a reason.

items.title: PH 2.0 mm connector
items.body: The first board functioned as a battery adapter, but the connector and resulting assembly were too large for the intended glove packaging.

items.title: SH 1.0 mm connector
items.body: I reduced the connector pitch and produced the version that fit the available space correctly.

items.title: Integrated charging
items.body: The final revision retained the smaller connection and added the battery-charging circuit to complete the interface.

title: Box Turtle AFC BTIO
subtitle: A connector board adapted to my wiring
summary: I redesigned the Box Turtle AFC BTIO board in EasyEDA Pro so its connectors matched the layout required by my installation.

content.body: My contribution was deliberately narrow: I took a simple existing interconnect function and redrew the board around the connector choices and cable arrangement I actually needed.

content.title: Completed adaptation
content.body: The replacement board resolves the connector mismatch without changing the wider Box Turtle AFC system.

title: ESP32 Lamp
subtitle: A movable tower-crane lamp powered through PCB rails
summary: I built a multi-axis lamp shaped like a tower crane, with an ESP32 controller, V-roller motion and cable-chain-free power delivery.

content.body: The mechanical form follows a tower crane: V rollers travel along 2020 extrusion so the light can move through the working area. I avoided a conventional cable chain by passing power through custom PCB interconnects and rails that act as a linear slip contact.

rows.label: Rails
rows.value: Linear power delivery along the extrusion

content.body: The end effector combines approximately 2500 K and 6500 K LED arrays. Sliding across the capacitive control blends the two channels to select a colour temperature between them.

items.title: Rushed STM32 board
items.body: The first controller revision was STM32-based and failed outright before it could become a dependable platform.

items.title: ESP32 conversion
items.body: The second board moved control to an ESP32 and operated, but I had selected the external buck-converter module incorrectly.

items.title: Custom power circuitry
items.body: I replaced the unsuitable module with a purpose-designed power stage, producing the final working electronics.

content.title: Release state
content.body: The lamp is complete; I plan to publish the release material later.

title: NFC Reader
subtitle: Card UIDs delivered as ordinary keyboard input
summary: I built an NFC reader that identifies a tag and types its UID through a USB HID keyboard interface.

content.body: The device presents itself as a standard keyboard, so scanning a card places the identifier directly into whichever text field has focus. That keeps the reader independent of a custom desktop driver or application.

content.title: Input path
content.description: A scan becomes text through a short device-side pipeline.
items: Send the characters as HID keyboard events

title: Custom Tool Changer
subtitle: Five independent direct-drive tools on one printer
summary: I designed a custom printer that mechanically exchanges five CAN-connected direct-drive tools, each with its own heater and extruder motor.

content.body: The complete machine frame was designed around tool changing rather than adapting a single carriage afterwards. Each docked tool remains an independent print head, allowing inactive heads to preheat and each one to stay configured for a different filament.

rows.label: Material range
rows.value: Independent soft, rigid and otherwise incompatible filaments

content.body: Tool retention uses a latch-and-pin mechanism. The carriage performs the mechanical lock and release without requiring separate actuation electronics on the carriage itself.

content.title: Feature complete
content.body: The five-tool exchange works, but refinement and wider machine integration keep the project active.

title: EPaper Calendar
subtitle: A USB-powered tri-colour display with browser uploads
summary: I built an ESP32 e-paper display that serves a local upload page and converts images for a 240 × 360 black, red and white panel.

content.body: When connected to USB-C power, the display hosts a webpage for choosing and converting an image. The ESP32 receives the prepared bitmap and updates the panel; it does not fetch calendar data by itself.

rows.label: Input method
rows.value: Image upload and conversion through a hosted webpage

items.title: Initial design
items.body: The first board used components that were unnecessarily small for hand assembly and made the build impractical.

items.title: Assembly and power redesign
items.body: I revised the component choices and corrected the power problems, producing the finished working display.

title: Digital Signage
subtitle: Central scheduling for browser-based local displays
summary: I built a Flask signage server that centrally schedules images and video across Android screens running full-screen browsers.

content.body: Each display is deliberately thin: an Android device opens the local signage page in a full-screen browser, while an Ubuntu server owns the media queue, schedules and device-wide control.

rows.label: Display clients
rows.value: Android signage screens with a full-screen browser

rows.label: Media
rows.value: Timed image queues and video playback

rows.label: Control
rows.value: Central management of all connected screens

content.body: Keeping the clients browser-based made replacement and expansion straightforward: the operational logic stayed on one server instead of becoming forty slightly different applications.

title: Tide Bound
subtitle: Fishing and exploration on a generated island
summary: I created a Unity 6 game about fishing, selling the catch and upgrading equipment on a procedurally generated island.

content.body: The project grew from a school hackathon theme based on the jungle. I expanded that starting point into an island whose terrain and forests are generated from noise, then added animals and a repeatable fishing economy.

rows.label: Economy
rows.value: Sell fish and purchase better rods

rows.label: Progression
rows.value: Continue until every available upgrade is obtained

title: Celestial Feasts
subtitle: A pizza economy drifting through space
summary: I made a school-hackathon game where the player gathers limitless ingredients on a dome, sells pizzas and earns a rocket escape.

content.body: The hackathon theme combined food with the galactic. I interpreted it as a small resource-and-crafting loop on a spaceborne dome, where the surrounding world is absurdly generous but the ticket home still has a price.

rows.label: Resources
rows.value: Infinite ingredient sources around the dome

rows.label: Win condition
rows.value: Reach 1,000 and leave in the rocket

title: Raspberry Pi Hologram
subtitle: A compact prism display on a Pi Zero breakout
summary: I designed a Raspberry Pi Zero breakout with a 1.3-inch IPS display and RTC for a glass-prism hologram illusion.

content.body: The PCB places a small square display directly on the Pi Zero and provides real-time clock hardware for timekeeping. A transparent prism cube sits above the panel and reflects prepared imagery into a floating four-sided illusion.

rows.label: Optical element
rows.value: Glass prism cube above the screen

title: Automatic Chess Robot
subtitle: A digital study of sensed chess-piece movement
summary: I planned an automatic chess board in CAD and code, using reed switches for piece detection and scripted movement paths.

content.body: I developed the mechanical layout and the code needed to plan board movement, with a reed-switch grid intended to identify occupied squares. The design never progressed into physical assembly.

content.title: Stopped at the digital stage
content.body: I ended the experiment after buying a Chestnut automatic chess set that already met the practical need behind the project.
